content.text_value: An AI-first asset management transformation journey

rows.label: WHY
rows.sublabel: now is the right time to act
rows.body: The industry grew 11% to $147T AUM in 2025, but 80%+ of revenue growth came from market performance while fee compression continues at 1–3% a year. **Agentic AI will disrupt the industry, and it rewards quick, thoughtful action.**

rows.label: WHAT
rows.sublabel: an AI-first manager will look like
rows.body: **Rebuilt with AI at its core:** research coverage up 2x to 5x, client coverage per relationship manager up to 3x, and 55–65% of operations capacity released — 300 to 500 bps of value across the P&L.

rows.label: HOW
rows.body: Three plays — **Deploy** (table stakes), **Reshape** (value concentrates), **Invent** (new models) — starting with two or three workflows reimagined end to end and owned by the business.

content.text_value: AI lets asset managers capture significant value

rows.label: Smarter
rows.body: 2x-5x research coverage and 5-15% Sharpe ratio improvement. Research agents deliver overnight what used to take weeks.

rows.label: Closer to Clients
rows.body: 3x-5x client coverage per relationship manager and 5x-10x RFP capacity; personalization at scale for segments too small to serve.

rows.label: Faster
rows.body: 2x-3x speed to market for new products, 50-70% trade error reduction, and operations capacity up 55-65%.

rows.label: Leaner
rows.body: 25-30% net cost reduction over three to five years; negative operating leverage reversed.

rows.label: More Resilient
rows.body: Continuous compliance surveillance, AI risk monitoring and audit-grade transparency in agentic workflows.

content.text_value: Three ways to source each capability

rows.label: Adopt
rows.body: Commodity capabilities — document extraction, meeting notes, code assistants — bought from vendors and configured, not built.

rows.label: Adapt
rows.body: Differentiating workflows built on a shared platform with firm data, prompts and guardrails.

rows.label: Assemble
rows.body: Proprietary agents on the investment knowledge graph, where the firm's data is the moat.
